Return to Crestwood

Desktop and mobile design review

5 October 2026 · All eight pages: home, about, primary, secondary, school life, admissions, visit planner and privacy. Reviewed as a first-time parent using the site.

Stack: static HTML, vanilla JavaScript and CSS. Existing navy, sky-blue and amber tokens, Manrope headings and DM Sans body type were preserved. Project conventions: DESIGN.md and PRODUCT.md. The review uses the six better-interface domain skills.

Scope and coverage

DomainEvidence inspectedResult
AccessibilityAll pages, native controls, landmarks, image alternatives, labels, accessibility-tree names and roles, keyboard flows, reduced motion and forced-colour focus.Checked; heading and focus improvements implemented. Actual screen-reader speech not verified.
Layout320, 390, 720, 768, 1024 and 1440 CSS pixels. 720px tests reflow equivalent to a 1440px desktop at 200% zoom. Increased text spacing at mobile and desktop.No horizontal overflow in 48 page/width checks.
WritingNavigation, curriculum, admissions, activity controls, download feedback and planner disclaimer.Specific activity labels added. Planner limitation remains visible.
TypographyRendered mobile/desktop headings, wraps, body copy, input sizes and font declarations.Existing hierarchy retained; WOFF2 fonts added.
ColoursRendered colour contrast through axe-core WCAG A/AA checks and measured focus/text pairs.Two shared contrast failures corrected; no automated violations remain.
UI polishShared cards, photo crops, hover/press/focus states, tab selection, disclosures and modal interactions.Natural photo proportions restored and press scale standardised. Animation replay at 10% speed not verified.

Principles and models applied

These are practical heuristics, not a claim that every design theory has a universal pass/fail test.

PrincipleApplication
Gestalt proximity and similarityRelated text stays in a shared card or section; repeated school and activity cards use consistent styling.
Visual hierarchy and balanceOne page heading, clear section titles, quieter supporting copy and navy primary actions. Images balance text-heavy sections.
Fitts’s lawLarge menu and form actions; footer navigation targets enlarged to 44px high. Native date/select controls retained.
Hick’s law and progressive disclosureCore navigation stays concise. Curriculum tabs and FAQ disclosures limit simultaneous detail without hiding the next step.
Nielsen usability heuristicsConsistent navigation, visible selected tabs, Escape to dismiss overlays, download status, native date validation and plain planner limitations.
Recognition over recallVisible form labels, stage-specific checklists and descriptive activity controls.
Accessibility and responsive designSemantic HTML, named controls, visible focus, reduced-motion support, alternative text and stacked mobile layouts.

Verification

  • Node syntax check: node --check dist/app.js passed.
  • Playwright + axe-core: design-audit.cjs, 48 combinations, no WCAG A/AA automated violations after corrections.
  • Playwright rendering: review-render.cjs, 16 full-page desktop/mobile screenshots, plus 320px layout checks. No page errors, missing images or horizontal overflow.
  • Interaction checks: review-interactions.cjs passed mobile navigation, skip link, arrow-key tabs, FAQ, dialog Escape and focus restoration, checklist download, date validation and visit-plan download.
  • State checks: review-states.cjs passed text-spacing stress, keyboard focus, forced colours and reduced motion. Accessibility tree captured on mobile and desktop.

Not verified: real screen-reader speech; physical iOS/Android devices; RTL/localisation (English-only site); animation replay at 10% speed. No remote submission, loading or network-error states exist in this local planner. Automated checks do not establish complete WCAG conformance.

New image assets

Three illustrative images created with the built-in image generator, optimised as locally hosted WebP files with alternative text and lazy loading. They supplement the existing three photos.

  • reading.webp · Prompt: candid Nigerian pupils reading together at an accessible school-library table, navy/light-blue uniforms, natural light and realistic editorial photography.
  • creative.webp · Prompt: Nigerian primary pupils and a teacher making colourful collage and painting in a bright classroom, natural expressions and documentary photography.
  • sport.webp · Prompt: Nigerian secondary pupils doing a friendly outdoor basketball passing drill, navy/white sports clothing, greenery and natural afternoon light.

No image is evidence of an actual campus, facility or programme.

Final first-time visitor walk-through · 6 October 2026

Retested all eight pages at 320px, 390px and 1440px in a local Chromium render of the published source. All 24 page/width checks passed: no horizontal overflow, missing images, page errors or automated WCAG A/AA violations. Navigation, direct-page reload, browser Back, keyboard curriculum tabs, FAQ disclosures, activity dialog focus, checklist download, date validation and visit-plan download passed.

One issue was found and fixed: Escape could close mobile navigation while leaving focus on a hidden link. Focus now returns to the visible menu button. The same walk-through then passed on both tested mobile widths.

First-time parent assessment: the school stages and learning approach are easy to explore, and the visit planner clearly distinguishes preparation from a booking. Real contact information, location, fees and confirmed policies are still needed to complete a real admissions enquiry. Physical-device and live screen-reader testing remain unverified.

Verdict

Approve for the reviewed interface scope. No high-severity interface findings remain in the checks performed. The pages are brighter, consistent and usable in the tested desktop/mobile layouts. Verified school contacts, location, fees, policies and a real enquiry or booking service remain necessary for real admissions.
